newsitem.title: FRANCE: French sailor breaks round-the-world record.
newsitem.headline: French sailor breaks round-the-world record.

text.p: French sailor Olivier de Kersauson set a new round-the-world sailing record on Monday, circling the globe in 71 days, 14 hours, 18 minutes and eight seconds in his Sport-Elec trimaran yacht.
The previous record, set by New Zealander Sir Peter Blake three years ago, was 74 days 22 hours and 17 minutes.
De Kersauson and his crew of six crossed the finish line at 6.59 a.m. GMT, making them the winner of the Jules Verne trophy, offered for sailing around the world in under 80 days.

Named after author Jules Verne's 1872 novel Around the World in 80 Days, the race ends at an imaginary line across the English Channel between the southernmost tip of Britain's Lizard Point and France's Ouessant Island.

Prime Minister Alain Juppe, in the midst of a closely contested parliamentary election campaign, quickly issued a congratulatory message to de Kersauson expressing his admiration and adding, "We are all proud of what you have accomplished."

President Jacques Chirac, in a separate message, said the "extraordinary victory...confirms the very great talent of our sailors and brings to France a pride and elan that can only be achieved in the winning of a great challenge."
The conservative Chirac has urged a "new elan" and a "shared elan" for France in his campaign messages urging a victory for the governing centre-right.
Tens of thousands of fans were waiting to greet de Kersauson and his crew in the port of Brest, western France, which they left on March 4.
Blake, on his trimaran Enza-New Zealand, in 1994 broke a record of 79 days six hours and 15 minutes set a year earlier by France's Bruno Peyron on his trimaran Commodore explorer.
